claims.text: A Pt-based catalyst with a nanoscale textured, three-dimensional porous surface will have greater HER activity than a conventional smooth-surfaced Pt-based catalyst.
A Pt-based catalyst with a nanoscale textured, three-dimensional porous surface will have greater HOR activity than a conventional smooth-surfaced Pt-based catalyst.
A Pt-based catalyst with a nanoscale textured, three-dimensional porous surface will have greater operational durability than a conventional smooth-surfaced Pt-based catalyst.
Surface or interface engineering can induce a nanoscale textured or three-dimensional porous architecture on the catalyst surface.
The engineered nanoscale textured or porous surface increases the effective catalytic area.
The engineered structure increases the density of accessible active sites.
The engineered structure improves mass transport.
Improved mass transport reduces local concentration gradients.
The engineered structure minimizes catalyst surface degradation and corrosion.
The textured catalyst will exhibit a significantly lower HER/HOR overpotential than the smooth catalyst.
The textured catalyst will exhibit a higher HER/HOR current density than the smooth catalyst.
The textured catalyst will exhibit less performance decay over time than the smooth catalyst.
The proposed enhancement may diminish at very high temperatures or in highly aggressive electrolytes because the textured layers may degrade.
The magnitude of the gains depends on pore size, pore distribution, catalyst composition, surface-treatment parameters, and operating conditions.
